children: The UK unemployment rate fell to 4.7% in the three months to August 2026, defying market expectations that it would remain unchanged at 4.9% for the fifth consecutive period.

This marked the lowest reading since the three months to July 2025, as the number of unemployed people declined by 47 thousand from the previous quarter to 1.712 million, driven by decreases in those unemployed for up to 6 months and between 6 and 12 months.
Compared with the same period last year, the number of unemployed people fell by 26 thousand.

Meanwhile, total employment rose by 102 thousand from the previous period and by 356 thousand from a year earlier to 34.577 million, while the employment rate increased by 0.2 percentage points both quarterly and annually to 75.3%.
The number of people with second jobs increased in the latest quarter to 1.294 million, accounting for 3.7% of people in employment.
Lastly, the inactivity rate edged down by 0.1 percentage point from the previous quarter to 20.9%.

title: UK Jobless Rate Unexpectedly Falls
